name: Washington Dulles International Airport

runway.v: four runways; longest 1C/19C and 1R/19L, each 11,500 ft (about 3,505 m); 12/30 is 10,500 ft, 1L/19R 9,400 ft
runway.quote: 1C/19C 11,500 feet long and began service when Dulles opened in 1962.

customs.v: CBP clears arriving general aviation aircraft 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; call CBP before leaving the foreign airport and at least 2 hours before arrival; landing permission valid +/-30 minutes
customs.quote: Inspection services for the entrance/arrival of aircraft at KIAD are available 24 hours per day

handling.v: general aviation FBOs: Signature Flight Support (east side) and Jet Aviation (west side); CBP also lists Dulles Jet Center
handling.quote: Signature Flight Support and Jet Aviation serve as the Fixed Base Operators for the general aviation community.

hours.v: airport attended all months, all days, all hours (24 hours)
hours.quote: 2.3.1 All Months, All Days, All Hours

noise.v: engine run-ups 22:00-07:00 local need prior approval from airport operations; flight training 22:00-07:00 is prohibited
noise.quote: ENGINE RUN-UPS BTW 2200L & 0700L REQUIRE PRIOR APPROVAL FM ARPT OPS.

max_aircraft.v: airfield handles aircraft up to Group VI, such as the A380 and B747-8
max_aircraft.quote: capable of handling aircraft up to Group VI, such as an A-380 aircraft and B747-8 aircraft.

notes: Read the MWAA flydulles.com airport overview (undated) and the CBP KIAD fact sheet (17 Apr 2024, KIAD-0424). The flydulles noise FAQ page and FAA Chart Supplement (CS_NE_20260903.pdf) could not be opened. Metres are my conversion (1 ft = 0.3048 m). IATA code left null: the official pages read show only the FAA identifier, not a stated IATA code. 1 Nov 2026: read the FAA US AIP Part 3 AD 2 page for KIAD (filed under 'District of Columbia'; no edition date shown on the page). Added hours, fuel ('A' read as Jet A) and night run-up/training rules. The AIP runway table gives 01C/19C and 01R/19L 11500 ft x 150 ft, 01L/19R 9400 ft x 150 ft and 12/30 10501 ft x 150 ft (all runways 150 ft wide); the runway rule from flydulles.com is kept. The AIP also limits some taxiways by wingspan (e.g. taxilane A between A1 and A5 not for wingspan over 118 ft; TWY E1 under 79 ft) and lists ARFF Index E.
